subject: SIG branching policy and parallel re-answer tracking
messages:
From: Jane Doe <jane.doe@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire changes — proposed approach for parallel re-answers

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for running the initial SIG review for Nimbus Health. We've finished an internal pass and there are two things that make our audit tighter this quarter: (1) SIG just released a minor revision that touches about a dozen items (non-critical), and (2) a couple of answers Redwood provided in v21 will need clarifications that could change downstream evidence references.

Rather than redoing the whole questionnaire in-place, our security team prefers a branching approach so we can track diffs and re-answers separately for audit purposes. Can you confirm whether Redwood can: (a) create a parallel re-answer branch for v22 that preserves v21 as the canonical historical record, (b) provide a short CSV mapping of changed questions and evidence refs, and (c) indicate who internally will own the re-answers?

We have an audit window starting May 24 and would like to lock any final re-answers by May 20. Attached is a brief spreadsheet that lists the fields we flagged (I also pasted a sample row below).

Sample row: question_id=SIG-AC-12 | v21_answer=Yes | flagged_change=clarify-data-retention | suggested_evidence=policy_v2.pdf

Best,
Jane
Security Operations
Nimbus Health

Attachment: flagged-questions-sample.csv

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@nimbushealth.com>, security@nimbushealth.com
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 9 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire changes — proposed approach for parallel re-answers

Jane — thanks for the clear ask. I like the branching idea; it aligns with how we handle schema changes internally and keeps a clean audit trail. Quick answers up front: yes to (a) and (b); for (c) Redwood will assign ownership as follows: Marcus will be SIG re-answer lead, Monica will coordinate evidence uploads and diffs, and I will be primary point for the audit lock and communication.

Proposed timeline:
- Today (May 9): we create a v22 branch and upload a change-tracking CSV.
- May 10–14: internal review & draft re-answers (Marcus / product security)
- May 15–18: evidence collection and finalization (Monica)
- May 19: submit v22 to Nimbus for review
- May 20: finalize and lock responses

I attached our proposed branching policy doc and the re-answer matrix template to make this as frictionless as possible. If the audit window is firm on May 24 we'll be able to deliver.

Next step: I'm scheduling a 30-min sync for Tuesday May 11 at 10am PT to walk through the CSV diff format and ownership. Can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG-branching-proposal.pdf, SIG-v22-reanswer-matrix.csv

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, Jane Doe <jane.doe@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: monica.patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 08:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire changes — proposed approach for parallel re-answers

Laura / Jane — I ran a quick gap analysis on the flagged items and a handful are clarifications rather than substantive changes. Operational notes:

- Branch semantics: create branch name "SIG/v22-nimbus-reanswers" and preserve v21 in the archive bucket (read-only).
- Re-answer policy: mark any re-answered question with metadata: reanswer_id, reanswer_owner, reanswer_date, evidence_refs (we'll store refs to S3/Drive).
- Diff CSV: we'll populate question_id, v21_answer, v22_draft_answer, evidence_key, notes. Monica will publish the first draft by EOD May 11.

I'll own technical sign-off on the answers and will escalate any substantive changes back to product. Monica — can you confirm you'll have the evidence keys and share a link to the Drive folder once uploaded?

On availability — Tuesday 10am PT works for me.

Marcus Lin
Director, Trust & Safety
Redwood Inference
